source.title: Van Criekinge et al. · Full-body optical gait recordings
source.authors: Tamaya Van Criekinge, Wim Saeys, Steven Truijen, Luc Vereeck, Lizeth H. Sloot, Ann Hallemans
source.acquisition: Barefoot overground walking at self-selected speed, recorded using 100 Hz Vicon Plug-in Gait.
source.processing: Each stride spans consecutive source-labeled right foot strikes and includes one right toe-off. Marker and fitted segment trajectories are sampled at 101 phase points. Source knee flexion, pelvis displacement, pelvis travel speed and pelvis-relative wrist excursions are reported in original subject units.
source.retargeting: Recorded optical segment axes, joint-center directions, radial/ulnar wrist landmarks and Vicon hand centers derived from the third metacarpal markers orient the bones of the shared display model. Arm and hand motion is specific to each recorded side. Bone lengths are fixed and horizontal travel is scaled to model leg length. Both ankle targets follow their measured lateral tracks relative to a common pelvis origin. Measured knee centers guide knee bend around each hip-to-ankle line. A temporally regularized two-link leg fit balances tracked ankle positions and knee flexion while grounding the bony sole during stance. Swing foot height follows the lower heel/toe marker relative to its contact baseline. Toes and rearfoot share a rigid segment, the patella follows the femur, and skull and fingers follow torso and hand respectively.
